name: Test Before Shipping
description: Run the full test suite before claiming work is done — no shipping untested code.
content:
# Test Before Shipping Rules

- Run the full test suite before every commit — `npm test`, `pytest`, `go test ./...`, or your project's test command
- Don't skip tests to save time — a 2-minute test run is cheaper than a production bug
- If tests fail, fix them before committing — never commit with known test failures
- Run both unit tests and integration tests when available — unit tests alone don't catch integration issues
- If E2E tests exist, run them before marking a feature complete — they catch real user-facing bugs
- Check test coverage for new code — new features should have tests, not just pass existing ones
- Run the linter alongside tests — type errors and lint violations are bugs waiting to happen
- If a test is flaky, fix it or mark it as known-flaky — don't just re-run until it passes
- Run tests in the same environment as CI — local-only passes that fail in CI waste everyone's time
- When fixing a bug, write a test that reproduces it first — then fix the bug and verify the test passes
- If you change a test to make it pass, make sure the change is correct — weakening assertions hides bugs
- After merging, verify CI passes on the merged result — merge conflicts can break tests that passed individually
